finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: attacker-supplied POST 'feed' is passed directly to file_get_contents, which fetches arbitrary HTTP(S) URLs and also accepts file:// and php:// URIs. The response only reveals strlen of the body, so the finding is blind with a length oracle.

trace.note: Guard is only REQUEST_METHOD === 'POST' && isset($_POST['feed']); require_admin() is not called on this path
$xml = file_get_contents($_POST['feed']); raw attacker value reaches the stream layer
echo strlen($xml): only body length is returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No authentication (require_admin not called on this branch). No scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/link-local IP blocklist, no DNS pinning, no redirect control. file_get_contents follows HTTP redirects by default. Impact depends on allow_url_fopen and runtime config.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only condition on the path is `$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST' && isset($_POST['feed'])` at import.php:11, which is not an authentication, host, or scheme check. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is only called on the set_webhook branch (import.php:18), not on this one. session_start() at line 2 does not gate anything.
verdict.reason: import.php:12 passes the unauthenticated `$_POST['feed']` straight into file_get_contents with no scheme or host restriction, reached only through the guard at import.php:11, and import.php:13 returns just strlen($xml), so the SSRF is blind with a length oracle as claimed.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: the authenticated admin's set_webhook URL is passed unvalidated to curl_init and curl_exec. Default libcurl protocols include file://, and the response body is discarded, so the finding is blind.

trace.note: curl_exec($ch): request issued; CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION not set, so no redirect following
echo "ok": response body is not returned (blind)

finding.guards_checked: Admin session check via require_admin (empty() test, so any non-empty is_admin value passes). No URL scheme, host, or IP validation. No CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction. No CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION, so redirects are not followed.

verdict.guard_found: none closing. require_admin() (import.php:4-9) is a session check, not a URL validation guard, and it is the only gate. No scheme, host, or CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS restriction exists on the curl path (import.php:20-22).
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code (import.php:17-23), but the source is admin-only: $_POST['set_webhook'] is reached only after require_admin() (import.php:18) rejects any session without a non-empty $_SESSION['is_admin'], and the only occurrence of is_admin in the directory is that check (import.php:5), so no low-privilege attacker can reach the sink; the finding is an admin-only input, which the rubric says does not count.
